The current H04/H05/H10 attribute-heavy grid is 1,024/2,048/4,096/8,192 unique attributes per start tag in both native splits, with a literal output oracle. Each fixture is bounded to 4 MiB HTML and 8 MiB JSON, with a 16 MiB aggregate JSON cap enforced by forecast and pre-write admission. One Windows feasibility run at 8,192 attributes completed 250 samples plus 10 warmups in 49.9 seconds without a paired comparison; 16,384/32,768 at that sample shape and a 252,602-attribute single parse exceeded the 180-second timeout. These adversarial results do not establish Linux physical peak memory or a production capacity threshold.

Pinned html5ever 0.39.0 scans the accumulated tag attributes when checking each new attribute for a duplicate; unique-attribute input therefore has a derived quadratic comparison path. The safe main workload grid stops at 8,192; larger counts require a separate parser/containment comparison and remain outside the main confirmation grid.

HTML5 parity/rejection has local focused fixtures only; Linux RSS, tokenizer/attribute peak memory, representative conformance/gold adjudication, foreign ownership/failure controls and complete caller-to-output/drop measurement remain unverified
